summary.title: Space Invaders from Scratch - Part 2
summary.one_liner: You learn how to render a CPU-side pixel buffer to an OpenGL window using a fullscreen-triangle vertex shader, a fragment shader, and a texture, then draw a bitmap alien sprite on it.
keywords: how to draw a sprite in opengl
takeaways: Pixels can be stored in a CPU buffer of uint32_t values and uploaded to the GPU as a texture each frame.
A fullscreen triangle can be generated in the vertex shader using gl_VertexID, so no vertex data is needed.
The fragment shader samples the buffer texture to output colors to the screen.
A 1-bit bitmap sprite can be drawn into the buffer at a given position and color, with bounds checks.
summary.summary: The post is part 2 of a series building a Space Invaders clone in C++ with minimal dependencies. It explains why rendering is done on the CPU into a pixel buffer, then sets up OpenGL 3.3 shaders, a VAO, and a GL texture to display that buffer across a fullscreen triangle. It ends by defining a 1-bit Sprite struct, drawing an 11x8 alien bitmap in red over a green background, and updating the texture each frame with glTexSubImage2D.
